titre: LEGO Announces 4 New Sets Based on the Harry Potter HBO Series
extrait: The LEGO Harry Potter theme has been a mainstay since the first set came out in 2001. Now that HBO has a new TV adaptation of the Wizarding World in the works (set to debut on December 25), LEGO has finally unveiled a new batch of sets based on the new series. Four new sets have been announced, two of which are available to preorder now. They're all out January 1. Let’s take a look. The four sets offer a nice selection of characters and locations from the first book, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which is what the HBO show’s first season adapts. Honestly, these sets don’t look all that distinct from the sets based on the movies. Then again, based on the TV show’s trailer, they didn’t really change much when adapting the franchise into a show. It all starts on 4 Privet Drive. That’s where we find the home of the Dursley family, who adopt Harry Potter after you-know-who kills his parents. The Dursleys aren’t very nice to Harry, but this LEGO set lets you build their two-story house, complete with Harry’s cupboard under the stairs. This one’s available for preorder now. The three main young wizards all end up in house Gryffindor, so they spend a lot of time in the common room. This set recreates that cozy space, complete with a fireplace, five minifigures, and a Quidditch table that’s unique to the show. There are so many now-iconic things in the first book that it must have been hard to pick what to base sets on. That said, it would be a shame if there wasn’t a new Hogwarts Express set. This set has platform 9¾, plus the bold red train. It also includes minifigures for Harry, Hermione, Ron, Draco Malfoy, and Molly Weasley — all characters that appear in or around the train in the book. BrickHeadz are kind of like LEGO’s take on Funko Pops. They depict known characters from pop culture, but in a stylized design, and they’re meant for display. These seem like good, blocky renditions of the trio they depict. For more, check out all the best LEGO Black Friday deals available now. And take a gander at our running list of every upcoming LEGO set announced so far. Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. The first HBO Lego Harry Potter sets have been revealed, and they're remaking some classic kits... but fans aren't all enthused by the result. After being teased earlier this year, the initial wave of Lego Harry Potter kits based on HBO's new series revisits some old haunts; the lineup includes the Gryffindor Common Room, the Hogwarts Express, and Privet Drive. These include new designs and minifigures based on the TV show, but there are obviously similarities to what we've seen before – and that seems to be a sticking point for some. In a Reddit post discussing the sets, the top comment notes that they "they look like bootlegs of the originals lol." While there's positive feedback as well (particularly toward Privet Drive's faux-Tudor design), I'm finding just as many negative responses on social media after a quick look through the likes of Instagram. These sets are clearly dividing the community, and I can't imagine it's the reception Lego was hoping for. Here are the kits themselves: The Gryffindor Common Room is a constant throughout the Potter stories, so it makes sense that Lego would remake it here in its new HBO form. This one is made up of 738 pieces, comes with five minifigures (Harry, Ron, Hermione, Parvati, and Lavender), as well as lots of little details on almost every surface.UK: £79.99 at Lego This is probably the most unique of the sets, as the faux-Tudor exterior is quite different from the old movie version. The kit has 545 pieces and four minifigs to go with a brick-built '90s car – Harry, Uncle Vernon, Aunt Petunia, and Dudley. UK: £54.99 at Lego What with Harry's first trip to Hogwarts being such a pivotal moment in the story, it makes sense that the Hogwarts Express would feature as a major new set.
